clue.text: Its owner gains impressions of many countries

definitions.text: Its owner gains impressions of many countries

parts.words: Its owner gains impressions of many countries
parts.note: the impressions are not memories of travel but printed postage issues from abroad, collected and mounted in a book

explanation.surface: A seasoned traveller comes home with vivid memories of many lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector's book holds postage issues gathered from nations around the world.

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling miserable
a bell is something that clangs

explanation.surface: Someone has made an embarrassing blunder, a truly dreadful gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' and 'clanger' are both British slang for a blunder, but here a bloomer is a flower and the clanger a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that blooms is a flower, and this woodland plant is a spring flower.

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor reads the hospital notes and judges them trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the medic reading the notes, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A truthful, upright person is someone you can trust and rely upon.

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so it rises

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone notes an accurate reading of the rise in a current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reads TIDE from bottom to top in this down entry, giving the letters in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct text is to revise it, as a newspaper editor does.

clue.text: Bathers do it if they can't stand swimming

definitions.text: Bathers do it if they can't stand swimming

parts.words: Bathers do it if they can't stand swimming
parts.note: can't stand looks like disliking swimming, but means being out of their depth with feet unable to touch the bottom

explanation.surface: Some bathers just loll about because they hate having to swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying upright in deep water by moving the legs is what swimmers do when out of their depth.

definitions.meaning: the valve or pedal controlling fuel flow to an engine
to strangle someone by the neck

explanation.surface: A learner driver is unsure which control is which.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the engine's fuel control and the act of strangling.

clue.text: Enemy Zulu leader going round causing ferment

indicators.note: the letters go round in a whirl, rearranged into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Zulu chief circles an enemy force, stirring up unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' picks Z from Zulu; 'going round' shuffles ENEMY with Z into the answer. 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferment is an old word for an agent of fermentation, which is what this biological catalyst is.

definitions.meaning: a kind or class of thing
printed characters, as in printing blocks

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sort out the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a kind and the printed characters set by a compositor.

parts.note: tall means high
an order is a command

explanation.surface: The military top brass are questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests army chiefs, but a tall order is a lofty command, one that is hard to carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding request is an instruction pitched very high, so it is difficult to meet.

parts.note: spelt out as a phrase they make a word meaning convenient

explanation.surface: Someone finds a location handy for reaching the Hungarian frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The borders of Hungary are 'H and Y'; written as one word, that phrase means convenient.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conveniently placed or useful is near to hand.

clue.text: Mother strangely sweet on famous film-star

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: strangely says the letters appear in an odd, altered order

explanation.surface: A mother is oddly sweet on a celebrated movie star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' is the anagram signal and 'on' a link. The film star was a 1930s Hollywood actress famed for innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a celebrated Hollywood actress known for risqué one-liners.

clue.text: Churchman gets a pass, yet goes astray

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off the proper course, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A clergyman is given a pass but still wanders off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchman' suggests a priest, but this is a lay assistant at the altar; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant at the altar in church services is a minor churchman.

clue.text: Addle-pated fellow who ought to know better

definitions.text: fellow who ought to know better

indicators.note: to addle is to muddle or confuse, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A muddle-headed man should really have known better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Addle-pated' looks like one word meaning foolish, but 'Addle' muddles PATED. The definition is wry: an expert should know better than anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert, skilled person is the one who really should know best.

clue.text: Guns of a size worth ordering

indicators.note: ordering means putting the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Artillery pieces are sorted by size and value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges the nine letters of SIZE WORTH; 'of a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: These are short-barrelled artillery pieces that fire shells at a high angle.

indicators.note: after puts the first piece behind the outlaw in the answer

parts.note: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw
a wink signals shared knowledge or complicity

explanation.surface: An accomplice gave a knowing look after a criminal was led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOD is Robin Hood, the legendary English outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tricked or deceived is to be led astray.

clue.text: Grew silent, becoming too hot to talk

indicators.note: becoming says the letters turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone fell quiet because the heat had become unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges the ten letters of GREW SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppressively hot weather leaves people uncomfortable and listless.

clue.text: Thunder from a clear sky is something unexpected

definitions.meaning: literally a lightning strike with no clouds about
figuratively a sudden shock or surprise

explanation.surface: A thunderclap from a cloudless sky comes as a total surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a sudden surprise, from the image of lightning out of a clear sky.

clue.text: Hesitated to have the key changed

parts.note: F is a musical key
altered means changed

explanation.surface: A musician paused before modulating to another key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble or waver in action or speech is to hesitate.

parts.note: it looks like a fracture from a fall, but in cricket an over is six balls, and this is a ball that spins

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fracture was suffered while rolling over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler delivers an over of six balls; a spin delivery turning from the leg side has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket delivery that turns from leg to off is spun, so it is received in a turning over.

definitions.meaning: a gardener cautiously predicting that a plant might come into bloom
a common name for the hawthorn, which blossoms in late spring

explanation.surface: A plant nursery owner hedges a prediction about a hedgerow shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn takes this name from the month in which it usually blossoms.

indicators.note: ends picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A yearly vacation always seems to finish before it should.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual means occurring once every twelve months.

definitions.meaning: the verb expressing that something could happen

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if strength is merely a possibility.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a modal verb of possibility and a noun for strength.

parts.note: losing it looks like losing one's temper, but means losing the faculty of recall itself

explanation.surface: Someone who flies into a rage forgets about it afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Without the faculty of recall, a person cannot remember anything, including its loss.

clue.text: I daren't exchange one car for another

indicators.note: exchanging letters means swapping their places around

explanation.surface: A nervous driver dares not swap their car for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges the letters of I DAREN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing over an old car as part payment for a new one is this kind of deal.

parts.note: a dedication in a book opens with the word 'to' before the recipient
an egotist thinks first of himself, the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A vain author dedicates a book to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A vain author dedicates the book to himself; 'for a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy volume.

clue.text: Possibly married one who thought a lot of another

definitions.text: one who thought a lot of another

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A suitor is perhaps wed to the one they highly esteemed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the letters of MARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds another in high regard is a fan or devotee.

indicators.note: on means placed after, as in a down entry the second piece sits below
turns says the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Something turns against an adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is not a pronoun here but two letters for the reversal; 'turns' and 'on' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against something is an opponent of it.

clue.text: Shelter behind me in an affray

indicators.note: behind places the shelter after the other piece

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover behind me during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in an' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused, noisy fight among many people is an affray.

clue.text: Have a mind to have a party

definitions.meaning: to consider or be willing to accept an idea
to host guests at one's home

explanation.surface: Someone is in the mood for throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: One may consider an idea or host guests, both senses of the word.
